reviews.title: This is the "NZXT at home" of Fishtank cases
reviews.comment: Incredible airflow considering the way the case is designed.  PCCooler is basically like the "generic OEM" for a lot of parts in China.  If you have an NZXT H5/H6/H7, it's obvious a lot of corners were cut to make this case hit the below $50 price point, but there's nothing wrong with that.  If you come in expecting a budget case, you will get great value for your money. The packaging is very utilitarian - it comes in a box and has two styrofoam supports - and that's it.  Nothing else.  The case comes plain with no other extra packaging except a plastic bag covering it. You will find a 5 page manual inside the case and a bunch of "spare" parts/accessories.  Screws for hard drives, additional hexagonal standoffs for your mobo, etc. You can tell a lot of corners were cut to make it work, but for a beginner budget PC builder this case is more than enough - installation for everything was a breeze as the dual chamber "fishtank" design makes cable management easy and painless. Just beware that the PCI-E covers are PUNCH OUTS and not true covers - once you remove them there is no way to put them back on easily.  Hint: if you have a modern GPU, only punch out the second and third from the top of the case. Doesn't come with fans and has no RGB, not a big problem.  If you've worked with other modern builds this should be very familiar to you. The case does not give you threaded screws for fans, but most fans come with them as part of the purchase, so start digging your pockets or help from computer guys for them. The metal is much thinner, but this might be a good thing because it makes the case VERY light.  Only room for 1 3.25 HDD and one 2.5 SSD.  This case would be ideal for a MicroATX build.  The motherboard back side panel of the case (to your right if you were looking at the front of the case) also screws on via traditional thumb screws, whereas the front side can be easily pulled off using clips. No preinstalled straps for cable management - they just give you a few very thin twist ties. No removable magnetic mesh on the bottom intake/exhaust, only on the top. I could go on, but that's what you pay for a budget build - if you're a beginner use a lot of these won't be a big deal for you.
reviews.author: M. Park

reviews.title: great buy on sale....dont pay full price for it.
reviews.comment: Pretty nice case overall, missing some minor things like gromet covers, wider gaps and holes under motherboard better GPU power running, it looks dumb coming from the giant side gromet. PCI slot cover is janky as can be, I hate it and it sucks lol case metal is a tad thin but it work fine, seems sturdy when built out. Sure looks cool and seems to have decent airflow. Can fit a 360 rad on the side or top....my previous case could only do a 240. had no issue with Motherboard IO and PSU mounting, and plenty of space in back for cables to get tied up side glass panel works but the clips are pretty bad, feel like im going to break something taking it off most the time.
reviews.author: kellyrx8

reviews.title: Great case overall. Bad PCI covers
reviews.comment: This case is an excellent fish tank PC build with ample space for fans, and case management. Purchased during a sale and I think it was well worth the price as it comfortably fits my computer parts with space for cable management and room for future upgrades/growth. I didnt realize it came with an opening for a vertical GPU mount so it can work with many types if builds and have great airflow while doing so. The only issue I had was finding out the pci tabs are punch outs and not reusable but that isnt much of an issue.
reviews.author: Bruh.mp4

reviews.title: Spacious!
reviews.comment: This case is amazing. Everything fit perfectly with plenty of room to work in. I originally started my build in a smaller case and quickly realized I needed more space, so I ended up switching to this one. I just wish I had chosen it from the start. It’s super spacious, easy to build in, and had no problem fitting my oversized RTX 3080. Definitely a great choice if you want a hassle-free build with plenty of clearance. Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Richard Sanchez

reviews.title: Great Budget Case
reviews.comment: I got the case over others I preferred because I was low on funds after buying everything else. I went into the build sort of like ehhhhh this might work out. The case is a little thin and will flex somewhat until everything is in and screwed down. I loaded it up with 10 120mm fans. Running 6 as intake and 4 as exhaust. Three fan AIO is mounted at the top and will not fit on the side as they say. 140mm fans will not fit at the bottom as the edge of the fan comes into contact with the motherboard. However, even with the negatives I love the case. Has great air flow and stable temps. I run a Ryzen 9 7900x with a 9060 XT OC Edition and a 34 inch OLED and my temps are flat out awesome. GPU under load in COD never goes above 55c, case temp hovers around 28c max. I feel the wire management is great. I didn't have any issues with that at all. It's a cheap low budget case that will hang with others way above it's price range.
reviews.author: Warren L.
